tier_reason: The pillow-perf harness is public (testsuite/run.py, testsuite/cases/pillow_scale.py, wand_scale.py, pillow_blur.py, wand_blur.py, pillow_lut.py, wand_lut.py, auto/run.sh) and the data file names the CPU (Intel Core i5-4430, Ubuntu 18.04.3), but no compiler or compiler version is recorded and Pillow 7.0.0 is built with empty CFLAGS (distutils defaults), so it falls short of A; the benchmark belongs to the python-pillow organisation and was run by the Pillow-SIMD authors, so it is first-party (C).

corrections.workload: pillow-perf test suite: a 2560x1600 RGB image resized to 26x16, 320x200, 2048x1280 and 5478x3424 with Bilinear, Bicubic and Lanczos, RGB to L conversion, 3D colour LUT, Gaussian blur and JPEG load/save; Pillow 7.0.0 against ImageMagick 6.9.7-4 through Wand, both single-threaded (MAGICK_THREAD_LIMIT=1), median of 5 to 11 runs.
corrections.claimed_speedup: Core i5-4430, docs/src/data/i5-4430.json (derived from page data): Lanczos 2560x1600 to 320x200 40.46 ms for Pillow 7.0.0 vs 134.41 ms for ImageMagick 6.9.7-4 (3.3x); bilinear 15.83 vs 47.76 ms (3.0x); Lanczos upscale to 5478x3424 374.84 vs 1495.61 ms (4.0x); RGB to L conversion 5.25 vs 51.45 ms (9.8x); 3D LUT with a 4^3 table 111.19 vs 3353.63 ms (30x); blur radius 1 px 185.67 vs 675.34 ms (3.6x), 10 px 187.53 vs 1768.07 ms (9.4x), 30 px 186.41 vs 4090.08 ms (21.9x); JPEG load 21.39 vs 27.38 ms (1.3x). Same direction on the other three machines in docs/src/data (c5.large Xeon 8124M, m5a.large EPYC 7571, macbook.2019 Core i5-8279U): Lanczos to 320x200 2.2x to 3.1x, RGB to L 7.8x to 13.1x, 4^3 LUT 26x to 30x (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not fully stated: auto/run.sh builds Pillow 7.0.0 from source with python setup.py develop and empty CFLAGS (distutils defaults; the Pillow-SIMD builds add -msse4 or -mavx2); compiler and version not recorded. ImageMagick comes from Ubuntu's libmagickwand-dev package (auto/install_ubuntu.sh) through Wand, limited to one thread by MAGICK_THREAD_LIMIT=1 in testsuite/cases/wand.py.
corrections.caveats: The benchmark repository belongs to the python-pillow organisation and was written by the Pillow-SIMD authors (first-party, hence tier C); the compiler is not recorded. The ImageMagick baseline is the old 6.9.7-4 (Ubuntu 18.04 package, version given in docs/src/data/index.js), forced to one thread, and every Wand case clones the source image inside the timed region. Not all operations do the same work: Pillow's Gaussian blur is a three-pass extended-box approximation whose cost does not depend on the radius, while ImageMagick runs a true Gaussian (MagickBlurImage with radius 2.5r and sigma r), so the 3.6x to 21.9x blur ratios compare different algorithms; ImageMagick's grayscale conversion (setting the image type) need not match Pillow's L formula. Resizing (Lanczos/lanczos, Bilinear/triangle) and the 3D LUT (Color3DLUT against a Hald CLUT of the same 4^3, 16^3 and 36^3 sizes) are equivalent operations. Pillow-SIMD 7.0 AVX2 is about 4 to 7 times faster than plain Pillow at resizing in the same files (derived from page data). The libvips Speed-and-memory-use table includes only Pillow-SIMD, not plain Pillow.

notes: All numbers match the pillow-perf i5-4430.json rows for pillow-7.0 and imagemagick-6.9; the 6.9.7-4 version label is in docs/src/data/index.js. Language cannot be changed through verifier corrections: please set the language override to 'Python with C core' in decisions.json. Licence is MIT-CMU (pyproject.toml), a permissive HPND-style licence, so copyable stands.

tier_reason: The harness (bench/bench.m, bench/pngbench.m, bench/nbench.c), raw output (bench/results/results.txt, bench/results/m1.txt) and flags (Makefile: clang -O3 -march=native; libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2 built by scripts/get-deps.sh with -O3 -march=x86-64-v3) are public, but the main machine is only 'Intel i9 13th gen' with no SKU, the clang version is not stated, and the README says the 50 test photos are private and not in the repo, so the run cannot be reproduced; single-author first-party numbers are tier C, not A.

corrections.baseline: libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2 (TurboJPEG 3 API, SIMD, one thread) for JPEG; Wuffs (unpinned wuffs-unsupported-snapshot.c, decoding to BGRA) for PNG; libpng is not measured
corrections.claimed_speedup: Intel i9 13th gen, 50 private camera JPEGs, bench/bench decode-only from memory (bench/results/results.txt). Like-for-like on one thread: nitrojpeg to YUV planes 103.0 ms/image versus libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2 to YUV planes 107.4 ms (1.04x, derived from page data). All 16 threads versus libjpeg-turbo on one thread: nitrojpeg to YUV 11.7 ms versus 107.4 ms (9.2x, derived) and nitrojpeg to BGRX 24.7 ms versus libjpeg-turbo BGRX 124.1 ms (5.0x, derived). Apple M1 (43 photos, bench/results/m1.txt): one thread 153.8 versus 168.1 ms (1.09x, derived), 8 threads 30.4 versus 168.1 ms (5.5x). PNG, 34 real PNGs (938 MB, 805 Mpixel), bench/pngbench on the i9: nitropng parallel 45.5 ms versus Wuffs to BGRA 180.1 ms (4.0x, derived), but nitropng on one thread 222.6 ms is about 1.24x slower than Wuffs (derived); the README's headline table now reports 38 PNGs at about 43 ms versus Wuffs about 171 ms. Core i7-1260P (Arch Linux, 4 JPEGs): 5.4 ms parallel versus 32.3 ms on one thread, nitrojpeg only, no baseline.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang (Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS; version not stated) -O3 -march=native, plus -mbranches-within-32B-boundaries on x86 in the current Makefile and -fblocks off macOS; bench/bench is built with -DNJ_REFERENCE against a static libjpeg-turbo 3.1.2 that scripts/get-deps.sh builds with nasm SIMD, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release and -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 on macOS x86_64 (-mcpu=apple-m1 on arm64); Wuffs and pngbench are compiled -O3 with the same CPU flags.
corrections.hardware: Intel i9 13th gen, 8 cores / 16 threads, 48 KB L1D, 4 to 5.5 GHz, AMD RX 580, macOS (exact SKU not stated); Apple M1 MacBook Air 2020 (4+4 cores); Xeon E3-1245 v5 (Linux, nitro-only nbench numbers); Core i7-1260P (Arch Linux, different image set)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 0 stars, 1 fork; 82 commits, oldest visible commits dated 2026-09-27
corrections.caveats: The headline 9x to 11x compares nitrojpeg on all 16 threads with libjpeg-turbo on one thread and mixes output formats (11.7 ms is YUV planes, 124 ms is BGRX); the like-for-like figures are 1.04x on one thread (YUV versus YUV), 9.2x multi-threaded to YUV and 5.0x multi-threaded to BGRX. libjpeg-turbo gets no intra-image parallelism because camera JPEGs lack restart markers. The 50 test photos are private, the i9 SKU is not named and the clang version is not stated, so the numbers cannot be reproduced exactly; the machine's clock swings between 4 and 5.5 GHz (the author reports about 10 percent noise on single runs). The PNG baseline is Wuffs decoding to BGRA with checksums ignored, while nitropng outputs unfiltered rows (colour conversion is left to the GPU) and verifies Adler-32, so the work differs; on one thread nitropng is slower than Wuffs, and libpng is not in any table. Very new single-author repository (first commits 2026-09-27, 0 stars) whose README numbers change from day to day. nitrojpeg output is reported bit-identical to libjpeg-turbo's ISLOW IDCT on the 50 test images (bench/verify).

notes: Downgraded from A to C: CPU SKU missing, compiler version missing, private test set. The like-for-like single-thread result is parity (1.04x i9, 1.09x M1); the gain is intra-image parallelism, which the caveats now say plainly. The README PNG headline (38 PNGs, ~43 ms vs Wuffs ~171 ms) differs from the 34-PNG table still in the README and in m1.txt.

tier_reason: WangXuan95/Image-Compression-Benchmark is an independent third-party shootout (public RunBenchmark.py, Intel Core i7-12700H, Windows 10, every codec single-threaded) whose CLIC2021 and GDCC2020 tables hold HALIC v0.7.2 next to WebP lossless and PNG via Pillow 10.1.0; it cannot be A because HALIC is a prebuilt closed-source .exe with no compiler or flags.

corrections.caveats: The repository holds only README, LICENSE (MIT) and .gitignore; the releases (0.6.0 to 0.7.2) carry only Windows AVX/AVX2 .exe and static Linux binaries plus GitHub's automatic archives of that README-only tree, the author's HALIC-Image-Converter (GPL-3.0 Qt GUI) contains no codec source, and the benchmark's format table marks HALIC as not open source, so the code cannot be inspected or rebuilt and has_code is false even though the licence file says MIT. The measured binary is HALIC072e.exe/HALIC072d.exe from the benchmark's codec folder, with no compiler or flags. The PNG baseline is Pillow's zlib-based encoder (default level), not libpng, and WebP lossless also runs through Pillow 10.1.0 (method 1 and 5). The harness runs Pillow codecs in-process but launches HALIC as one process per image through os.system, so HALIC's times include process start-up and the comparison is conservative for HALIC. On tiny images PNG decodes faster (Kodak: PNG optimize=False 0.484 s versus HALIC 0.615 s), so the decode win shows only on large images. The benchmark author also wrote the competing NBLI/fNBLI codecs (fNBLI is smaller and decodes slightly faster than HALIC on CLIC2021). The author's own README charts carry no numbers.

notes: All quoted numbers match the HALIC, WEBP (lossless m1) and PNG (optimize=False) rows of the CLIC2021, GDCC2020 and Kodak tables, and the derived ratios are correct. No HALIC source exists in any public repository of the author; WebSearch snippets claiming source availability refer to the README-only repo. Last commit 2024-05-24 (LICENSE added), so stale is right.
